headline: Hawaii student finds fungi that break down plastic

sources.title: Fungi found on coconut husks can decompose plastic, sunscreen
Teen Discovers Coconut Fungi Can Filter Plastic and Sunscreen From Sea

chunks.text: A high school senior in Honolulu has found that fungi living on coconut [[husks]] can {{break down}} plastic. The same fungi also attack [[sunscreen chemicals]] and [[microplastics]]. Microplastics are tiny pieces of plastic that float in seawater. She {{teamed up with}} scientists at the University of Hawaii. Some of the fungal [[species]] she found did not {{show up}} in the world's largest gene [[reference database]]. That suggests they had never been [[described]] before.

verbs.correct: To separate a material into tiny pieces
verbs.wrong: To grow on the surface of something
verbs.why: Bacteria break down dead leaves in a garden, and the stomach breaks down food after a meal. The student found that fungi on coconut husks can break down plastic and sunscreen chemicals.

verbs.correct: To join others to do a job together
verbs.wrong: To give someone a job at a company
verbs.why: Two bakeries teamed up with each other for a food festival, and a singer may team up with a band for one album. The student teamed up with scientists at the University of Hawaii for the research.

verbs.correct: To appear in a place or a record
verbs.wrong: To try to make people admire you
verbs.why: A lost ring may show up under the sofa, and a late payment shows up on a bank statement. Some of the fungal species she found did not show up in the world's largest gene reference database.

chunks.text: The student first {{came up with}} the filter in her [[sophomore year]]. She {{put together}} the design from coconut [[byproducts]] like the [[fiber]]. For the shape, she {{drew on}} traditional Polynesian [[weaving]]. She then {{tried out}} the filter on [[surface water]] from the sea. It was able to {{filter out}} both sunscreen and microplastics. The filter does more than trap pollution. It also holds the fungi that can attack plastic.

verbs.correct: To create a new idea or plan
verbs.why: A chef came up with a new dessert for the menu, and a class can come up with a name for its pet fish. The student came up with the filter in her sophomore year.

verbs.correct: To make something by joining its parts
verbs.wrong: To delay an event to a later time
verbs.why: A father put together a crib from a box of parts, and a child can put together a model plane. She put together the filter design from coconut byproducts.

verbs.correct: To use something as a source of ideas
verbs.wrong: To prepare a written plan or agreement
verbs.why: A novelist draws on her own childhood for a book, and an architect may draw on old churches for a new library. For the shape of the filter, she drew on traditional Polynesian weaving.

verbs.correct: To test something to see if it works
verbs.wrong: To grow something in a laboratory
verbs.why: A driver tries out a car before buying it, and a cook may try out a new oven with a simple cake. She tried out the filter on surface water from the sea.

verbs.correct: To remove unwanted things from a liquid
verbs.wrong: To destroy a whole group of living things
verbs.why: A coffee machine filters out the grounds, and a home water jug can filter out chlorine. The student's filter was able to filter out both sunscreen and microplastics.

chunks.text: The student also {{looked into}} a natural [[compound]] called a [[tannin]]. She found that tannins can help {{narrow down}} which fungi attack sunscreen and plastic. Tannins in coconut fiber may also help those fungi grow. The goal is a natural way to {{clean up}} [[polluted]] seawater. But the work is still at an [[early stage]]. A school filter is a long way from a fix for the ocean's plastic problem. Much more testing would be needed before anyone could use it at sea.

verbs.correct: To examine a question or a problem
verbs.wrong: To keep a growing culture alive and fed
verbs.why: A manager looked into a customer's complaint, and a mechanic may look into a strange noise from the engine. The student looked into a natural compound called a tannin.

verbs.correct: To reduce a list to fewer choices
verbs.wrong: To make a plan or a rule weaker
verbs.why: A couple narrowed down the list of baby names to three, and a detective narrows down the suspects with each clue. Tannins can help narrow down which fungi attack sunscreen and plastic.

verbs.correct: To remove dirt or pollution from a place
verbs.wrong: To become sunny after rain or clouds
verbs.why: Volunteers cleaned up the park after the concert, and a city may clean up a river that factories once used. The goal of the student's filter is a natural way to clean up polluted seawater.

chunks.text: Her project {{stood out}} at the 2026 Hawaii state [[science fair]]. She took [[first place]] in [[microbiology]] and third place [[overall]]. She then {{went on to}} the international science fair in Arizona in May 2026. Her results are a promising first step, not a finished tool. Whether the idea could work at a larger scale is still an [[open question]]. For now, the fungi have only shown what they can do in a student's small experiments.

verbs.correct: To be easily noticed among others
verbs.wrong: To wait and be ready to help someone
verbs.why: A red coat stands out in a gray crowd, and one candidate stood out at the job interviews. The student's project stood out at the 2026 Hawaii state science fair.

verbs.correct: To continue to a later stage
verbs.why: The winner of the local race went on to the national final, and a nurse can go on to medical school. The student went on to the international science fair in Arizona in May 2026.

mainIdea.s: A Honolulu high school senior found that fungi on coconut husks can break down plastic and sunscreen. She built a seawater filter that uses them, and the early research won prizes at the state science fair.
mainIdea.why: The fungi attack plastic, microplastics and sunscreen chemicals, and her coconut filter took first place in microbiology at the 2026 Hawaii state science fair.

mainIdea.s: A Honolulu high school senior found that fungi on coconut husks can break down plastic and sunscreen. Her filter is now cleaning up beaches across Hawaii, and several cities have ordered their own copies.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the filter has only been tried out on surface water in a student project, and the work is still at an early stage.

mainIdea.s: Scientists at the University of Hawaii found that coconut palm trees can absorb plastic from polluted seawater. They plan to plant thousands of the trees along the coast to filter out microplastics.
mainIdea.why: The discovery was about fungi living on coconut husks, not trees, and it came from a high school student's research, not a planting plan.

lines.text: Did you see the story about a student in Honolulu? She found fungi on coconut husks that can {{break down}} plastic.
Fungi on coconuts? How does a high school student even find that?
She {{teamed up with}} scientists at the University of Hawaii. Some of the species did not even {{show up}} in the biggest gene database in the world.
So they might be new to science. [[You don't get that from a textbook]].
There's more. In her sophomore year she {{came up with}} a seawater filter that uses the fungi.
What did she use to make it?
Coconut byproducts. She {{put together}} the design and {{drew on}} traditional Polynesian weaving for the shape.
[[Old craft, new problem]]. Does it actually work?
She {{tried out}} the filter on surface water, and it was able to {{filter out}} sunscreen and microplastics.
Sunscreen too? I never wonder where that goes after a swim.
She also {{looked into}} tannins. They helped her {{narrow down}} which fungi attack the plastic.
So could this {{clean up}} the ocean?
Not yet. It's early research, and [[a school lab is not the open sea]].
Sure. Still, her project {{stood out}} at the state fair, right?
First in microbiology, third overall. Then she {{went on to}} the international fair in Arizona.
[[Give it a few years]]. She is going to be famous.
Maybe. Either way, [[the hard part starts now]]. Someone has to test it at a bigger scale.
True. Coconuts cleaning the sea. I would not have guessed that.
